_about: Hand-maintained homework for one game. Keys: event (overrides: venue, kickoff_text, kickoff_iso, tv, sub_title, kicker, deadline_text), consensus (a sportsbook line to compare with), research (the Homework section). Delete the file and the card still renders from Kalshi alone.

opener.source: VegasInsider matchup page and Lineups, Sep 18 2026
opener.spread: Reported four ways: Green Bay −6.5 (VegasInsider, Lineups), −5.5 (TheSpread, RotoWire), −4.5 (VegasInsider's own week page, PicksAndParlays). Every source agrees the direction was toward the Jets.
opener.moneyline: Green Bay −285 at the open, about −180 to −205 now

injuries.GB: OUT: DT Warren Brinson (calf). DOUBTFUL: DT Javon Hargrave (knee/concussion). QUESTIONABLE: EDGE Lukas Van Ness (concussion), CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), RT Zach Bako-Bewele (knee), LG Aaron Banks (knee). line.text: This line has been bet down hard. Every source agrees the direction — toward the Jets — even though they disagree on the magnitude, with reported openers of Green Bay −6.5, −5.5 and −4.5 all collapsing to −3.5, and Caesars alone hanging −3 at −118 on the key number. The moneyline compressed from −285 to roughly −185. The total went the other way, from 42.5-43.5 up through a 45.5 spike to 44.5.
line.kalshi: Kalshi has Green Bay at 62¢ ask, normalizing to 61.4%. The devigged sportsbook range is 62.0%-63.5%, with FanDuel the tightest single book at 3.98% hold giving 63.0%. So Kalshi is pricing Green Bay about one and a half to two points CHEAPER than the books — the only place on the weekend board where Kalshi is meaningfully softer than the sportsbooks on a favourite.
line.src: VegasInsider Sep 19; Lineups Sep 18; RotoWire Sep 15

splits.text: Spread: the Jets took 57% of tickets but 90% of the MONEY at DraftKings — called one of the week's most notable splits, with professional money heavily favouring New York on modest ticket volume.
Ticket distribution was nearly even but 85% of spread money was on the Jets. Bets and money on the total were split evenly.
splits.src: VegasInsider, quoted as of Thursday 9 PM ET, Sep 18 2026

splits.text: The dissenting reading: the Jets took 37% of bets and 47% of dollars — which on its own would imply no sharp lean at all.

line.conflict: The magnitude is wildly inconsistent — 90%, 85% and 47% of Jets spread handle from three sources — but the SIGN never flips: in every source that reports both, money share on the Jets exceeds ticket share on the Jets. A line moving one to three points toward the side with disproportionate handle but not disproportionate tickets is the textbook sharp-money signature. This is the single most important thing on this card, and it is why the two tracks part company here.

week1.head: Green Bay 0-1: lost 39-22 at Minnesota (Sep 13)
week1.text: Jordan Love threw for 387 yards and two scores on 21 of 42, and Christian Watson had 147 and two touchdowns — and Green Bay still lost by 17, outscored 22-0 in the fourth quarter by a Vikings team starting backup Carson Wentz. Nine explosive plays produced 22 points and one touchdown on four red-zone trips. That is the whole problem in a sentence. This is Green Bay's SIXTH STRAIGHT LOSS counting the end of last season and a wild-card exit. The Packers are also without their lead back AND their premier pass rusher — see the injury table.
week1.src: Vikings official box score Sep 13; Yahoo/Packers Wire Sep 18 2026

week1.head: New York 1-0: beat Tennessee 23-10 at Nissan Stadium (Sep 13)
week1.text: A wire-to-wire road win in Aaron Glenn's second season. Geno Smith was not sacked once, Breece Hall ran for 102, Garrett Wilson had six catches for 79, and the Jets held the ball for more than 38 minutes. The defence ranked second in the NFL at 195 yards allowed, generated pressure at the third-highest rate in the league and recorded three sacks, and led the NFL in special-teams EPA. A team that went 3-14 last season is chasing its first 2-0 start since 2015. The caveat the fanbase keeps raising: the secondary went all of 2025 without an interception, and it now loses Minkah Fitzpatrick.

injuries.read: The ledger favours the Jets and it is not close. Green Bay is missing Josh Jacobs and Micah Parsons outright, is probably without Javon Hargrave, has two offensive line starters questionable and two more players in concussion protocol. New York loses Minkah Fitzpatrick, which is real, and three rotational players. Neither quarterback is affected. This is a large part of why the market moved as far as it did.

weather.text: Rain, and enough of it to matter. The NWS point forecast for East Rutherford, updated 11:03 AM ET Sep 18, has a high near 71°F, SOUTH WIND 6-10 MPH GUSTING TO 20, and an 80% chance of precipitation — 'showers, with thunderstorms also possible after 5pm', with a quarter to a half inch of new rainfall. Weather.com via NJ.com says steady rain through the afternoon with heavy rainfall possible; FanDuel quoted an 83% chance. Wind at 6-10 mph is well below the roughly 15 mph threshold and is NOT a total-mover. The variable is the wet ball, and it points specifically at Green Bay, whose Week 1 identity was explosive downfield passing — seven completions of 20-plus yards. Green Bay's rookie kicker Trey Smack hit from 59 indoors last week and now faces MetLife in rain. One outlier to discard: footballdb lists 0% precipitation and contradicts the NWS and two other sources.
weather.src: NWS point forecast, updated 11:03 AM ET Sep 18 2026

venue.text: The Jets' home opener, promoted as a 'White Out' with white-on-white uniforms, in front of a fanbase chasing a 2-0 start for the first time since 2015. Garrett Wilson on the mood: 'That hasn't been our reality here, so I'm sure it might be a little extra.' Matt LaFleur called the Jets 'a complete football team' with no obvious weaknesses. Green Bay, by contrast, arrives on a six-game losing streak in what its own media is describing as a sour, urgency-driven spot.

voices.take: Roughly 20 named picks to 10: SI/MMQB 6-2, Bleacher Report 5-2 against the spread, Florio (Packers 24-13), Athlon's Cory Bonini, SI Betting's Peter Dewey (26-17), FanDuel Research, Yahoo/Packers Wire (25-19), PicksAndParlays and the Dimers model. NFL.com is the one major panel leaning Jets at 3-2, with Bergman, Kownack and Parr all projecting one-score New York wins.

voices.who: The models are MORE bullish on Green Bay than the price is
voices.take: Dimers, from 10,000 simulations, has Green Bay at 67.3% with a projected 24-19 and the Packers covering −3.5 in 55.1% of runs — though it also leans Under 44.5 at 51.9%. numberFire has Green Bay at 64%. Both sit above the market's devigged 62-63.5% and well above Kalshi's 61.4%. nfelo and ESPN's FPI could not be retrieved for this game.

Models, expert picks and the Kalshi price all lean Green Bay. The money and the line movement lean hard the other way, and so does the weather and the injury ledger. Every published total pick found was Under — Covers' Ed Scimia, PicksAndParlays and the Dimers model — with no Over picks at all. There is no honest way to make these agree; the two tracks resolve it differently and both say so on the record.

research.x_note: Reddit was unreachable — r/nfl, r/sportsbook, r/GreenBayPackers and r/nyjets all returned blocked — and no beat-writer X timelines were retrievable. Gang Green Nation and Acme Packing Company are both robots-blocked, though Acme's headline ('Green Bay should defeat Jets as road favorites') indicates the Packers blog's house view. The Jets-fan sentiment above comes from JetNation's Week 1 reaction thread and SI's Jets site: enthusiastic about the offensive line and Demario Davis, still nervous about the cornerbacks.

tracks.intro: Two of Ahmed's rows are picked by Claude, each by a fixed method, and placed through the same form as everyone else. Neither is the System: the System needs a live Pinnacle line and sits out until the collector runs.

research.method: Bet whatever most people think will win — sportsbook ticket counts, prediction-market crowds, expert panels, Reddit and X — at the best Kalshi price for that side.
research.verdict: Named analysts are 2-to-1 Green Bay and both available models are more bullish on the Packers than the market is. This track buys that. It should be said openly that the money disagrees: 85-90% of spread handle is on the Jets and the line moved one to three points their way. This track follows the crowd by construction — and the statistics track declined the game for exactly that reason.

evidence.text: Named picks run about 20-10 Green Bay: SI/MMQB 6-2, Bleacher Report 5-2 against the spread, Florio, Athlon, SI Betting, FanDuel Research, Yahoo, PicksAndParlays and the Dimers model.
Both retrievable models sit above the market: Dimers 67.3% with a projected 24-19, numberFire 64%. The market devigs to 62-63.5% and Kalshi to 61.4%.
Green Bay is the favourite at all eight books on the grid, −180 to −205, and put up 419 yards and 387 passing yards in a Week 1 loss.

The dissent, on the record: 90% of spread money at DraftKings and 85% at VegasInsider is on the Jets, the line moved 1-3 points toward New York, an 80% rain forecast works against Green Bay's downfield passing identity, and the Packers are without Josh Jacobs and Micah Parsons. This is the weakest of the six crowd positions.
evidence.src: RotoWire Sep 15; VegasInsider Sep 18; NWS Sep 18

evidence.text: Stake: 2,100 contracts at 62¢ = $1,302, fee $34.64, $1,336.64 tied up. Break-even 63.65¢ — note that is above the devigged market number, which is the cost of following a crowd into a price that has already moved.

statistics.method: Estimate each outcome's probability from models and the sharpest sportsbook prices, subtract Kalshi's ask and fee, and bet the line with the best expected profit — if there is one.
statistics.pick: No bet — sat this one out
statistics.verdict: Skipped, and this was the closest call among the skips. Kalshi's Green Bay at 61.4% IS about one and a half points cheap against the books — the only genuine softness found all weekend. But one and a half cents does not cover a 1.65¢ fee, and everything pointing at where the closing line is heading says the books' 63% is the stale number, not Kalshi's 61.4%. Buying a favourite at a small discount while 85-90% of the handle and the whole week's line movement run the other way is not an edge; it is being last through the door.

evidence.text: Moneyline: Kalshi Green Bay 62¢ normalizes to 61.4%. FanDuel at 3.98% hold devigs to 63.0%; the best-of-market synthetic (Fanatics −180 with DraftKings +170, 1.32% hold) gives 63.45%. So the gap is 1.0¢ to 1.45¢ — against a fee of 0.07 × 0.62 × 0.38 = 1.65¢ a contract. Net negative before any judgement is applied.

And the judgement makes it worse, not better. Three sources agree the Jets are the money side while tickets are roughly even, and the spread has moved one to three points toward New York all week. That says the books' 63% is trailing the market, so the 'discount' on Kalshi is likely to be closed by kickoff rather than paid out.
evidence.src: RotoWire Sep 15; VegasInsider Sep 18; Lineups Sep 18

evidence.text: The other side is no better. Kalshi asks 39¢ for the Jets, normalizing to 38.6%, against a book fair of 36.5%-37.0%. The Jets are the EXPENSIVE side on Kalshi — buying them here means paying about two cents over the books before the fee.

Spread: 'Green Bay by over 3.5' at 48¢ against a market-wide devigged cover of about 49.7% is a 1.7¢ gap against a 1.75¢ fee — zero. Kalshi's ladder is internally coherent too: the 9¢ step between the 2.5 and 3.5 thresholds implies a 9% chance of a three-point margin, which is a sane NFL key-number figure.

Total: 44.5 is a true pick'em at the books (Over 50.0%-50.5% devigged) and Kalshi asks 50¢ for the Over and 51¢ for the Under. The rain argues Under and every published total pick found was Under — but paying 51¢ for a 50% outcome and then a 1.75¢ fee is a losing trade however good the story is.
